prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1479; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped in traffic. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver of the claimed vehicle is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy period.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer noted the impact as minor, with no airbag deployment and both vehicles driven from the scene.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the claim. They show the rear bumper damage and the point of contact consistent with the described impact. A few old scratches on the lower panel may predate this loss and will be noted separately during the estimate review.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage has been inspected and the repair scope matches the impact as described. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the parties' statements and the physical evidence.

Entry 6: Claimant's recorded statement was taken through counsel. The account stayed consistent with the first notice of loss, though a few small details were added on this call, such as the seating position and the moment of braking.

Entry 7: Medical records reflect a diagnosis of neck and back strain. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury, and the severity of the claimed injury appears high relative to the low-speed impact. No prior injury to the same body areas is known from the records received so far.

Entry 8: Next steps are to request prior medical records, schedule an independent medical review, and obtain a final repair estimate before any evaluation of the bodily injury portion is made. File remains open pending these items.
